sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Bébinn is a name common in early Irish literature and legend. One Bébinn was a goddess of birth. She was sister of Bóand and mother of Fráech, Ireland's most handsome hero. Another Bébinn was a beautiful giant from Maiden's Land. She lived off the west coast and was always ringed by magical birds. She may once have been a goddess of pleasure. This Bébinn left the Otherworld for the king of the Isle of Man. She fled him when he began to beat her. The angry king pursued his wife and killed her.

okr.objective: Describe Bébinn as a goddess of birth and a giant of legend.
